summary.headline: Duroply Q4 FY26 revenue rose 5% YoY to ₹111.6 cr, but PBT fell to ₹1.03 cr after a ₹27.5 lakh wage-code exceptional loss and EBITDA slipped to ₹5.18 cr.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was ₹111.6 cr, up 5% YoY and 20% QoQ, with in-house manufactured goods at ₹61.9 cr (+4% YoY) and contract manufacturing at ₹49.7 cr (+6.7% YoY, roughly +50% QoQ). Gross margin fell to 34.3% from 37% in Q3 FY26 and 34.9% a year earlier, and EBITDA was ₹5.18 cr versus ₹5.4 cr in both Q3 FY26 and Q4 FY25. For FY26, revenue grew 8.3% to ₹402.6 cr, EBITDA rose 25.3% to ₹22.4 cr, and working-capital days improved across debtors, inventory and payables. Management said H2 FY26 growth slowed and that corrective actions are under way, while flagging high input-cost inflation linked to the West Asia conflict.

segments.name: In-house manufactured goods
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue ₹61.9 cr (+4% YoY, +2% QoQ); FY26 ₹224.9 cr (+2.3% YoY). Management said the premium and mid segments are both expected to grow low-to-mid double digits, after a hyper-growth phase in Tower product sales that has normalised.

segments.name: Contract manufacturing
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue ₹49.7 cr (+6.7% YoY, ~+50% QoQ); FY26 ₹177.7 cr (+17% YoY), driving most of the annual growth.

guidance_outlook: Targets a return to double-digit growth; management expects low-to-mid double-digit growth in both premium and mid segments going forward, with specifics withheld from the public platform.
Medium-term guidance: 10-12% volumetric growth plus price increases, implying roughly 9-12% quantitative growth over the next two years; management called this conservative given geopolitical risk.

Margin outlook for FY27 is uncertain; management hopes margins are not hit but expects any margin expansion to come at the EBITDA level, while cost-control steps and procurement under sufficient liquidity are being pursued.
EBITDA margin has risen from about 3.5% to about 5.5-5.6% and management believes it should keep improving over time.
Expects the organised share of the industry to gain as supply-chain disruption pushes demand away from unorganised players.
capex_capacity: No capex plan, capacity addition, utilisation figure or commissioning timeline was discussed on the call; the transcript contains no capacity or capex commentary.
Management did not disclose plant-level capacity or utilisation numbers; the only volume reference is a 10-12% volumetric growth target for the medium term, with price increases on top.
Plants in the Western part of India depend on imported raw materials, a cost point noted in Q&A, but no plant expansion or capex was announced.
demand_pricing: Cost increases from March and April were largely passed on to consumers, and May was partially passed on; management now sees market resistance to further price hikes.

Input costs are elevated: melamine, urea and phenol (petrochemical derivatives, about 40% of India's requirement sourced from Gulf countries) are costlier, and a weaker dollar and rising freight, fuel and labour costs add inflation.
Industry: about 70% unorganised and 30% organised; plywood industry grows about 6-7% a year and the organised segment about 10-11%.
Management expects a shift from unorganised to organised players after supply-chain disruption from the ongoing war.
Management is expanding the frontline sales force, reviewing loyalty programmes, and focusing on B2B and project sales in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What initiatives are being taken for growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Expanded frontline sales force to reach more customers across India, reviewing loyalty programmes with stakeholders, and prioritising B2B and project sales as a focus area for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of geopolitical tensions on the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Chemical input costs (melamine, urea, phenol) are elevated, the dollar has weakened, and freight, fuel and labour costs are rising, so high inflation is expected in the coming months; as a branded player, the company can pass on much of it but with limits.

qa_highlights.question: Have costs been passed on in April and May?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost increases from March and April were largely passed on, May partially; consumer resistance to further price increases is now emerging.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sector outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Plywood grows about 6-7% a year and the organised segment 10-11%; management sees a strong long-term 8-10 year outlook despite near-term input-cost pressure from wood, imported timber and petrochemicals.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins be affected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes not; it is working to control COGS and believes it can procure better given sufficient liquidity, aims for EBITDA margin expansion, but said raw material impact is hard to predict.

qa_highlights.question: Any quantitative guidance for the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly 9-12% quantitative growth over the next two years, made up of 10-12% volume growth plus price, described as conservative.

risks_watch: Gross margin fell to 34.3% in Q4 FY26 from 37% in Q3 FY26; watch whether input-cost inflation compresses FY27 EBITDA margins.
Consumer resistance to further price increases could limit pass-through of cost inflation and dent volumes.
H2 FY26 growth slowed, and management said corrective actions are needed; track whether Q1 FY27 growth returns to double digits.
Dependence on imported raw materials (timber, petrochemical-based resin chemicals) and currency movements.
Working-capital days fell sharply, notably payable days from 117 to 72; watch whether lower payables affect procurement terms or liquidity.
Employee costs at 12.2% of sales and the ₹27.5 lakh wage-code exceptional item.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near-term margins and demand: management openly said H2 FY26 was challenging and that input-cost inflation is hard to predict. It stayed more confident on medium-term volume growth and long-term sector prospects, while declining to disclose some specifics. Q&A ran with technical audio issues and several questions read out from the Q&A board.
key_quotes: Second half of the year was very challenging for us, and our growth rate saw a slowdown. We are taking necessary actions to correct this.

So maybe a 9 to 12% quantitative growth is what we would be looking at for the next two years. We are being very, very conservative on this, keeping in mind that there would be more geopolitical tensions coming our way, which could affect the demand situation within the country.
But for most parts, we have been able to. Any cost increase going further is going to now be a challenge.

growth.why: Management guides 9-12% quantitative growth (10-12% volume plus price) for FY27-FY28, but gives no capacity, capex or order-book numbers behind it and called the guide conservative, so backing is vague; Q4 revenue +5% YoY and EBITDA flat at ₹5.18 cr against ₹5.4 cr a year earlier.
